meta.theme: Stoic lessons on accepting what you can't change
meta.title: 5 Stoic lessons on accepting what you can't change

beats.text: Five Stoic lessons for accepting the things you cannot change.
One. Separate the situation from your opinion of it. The pain is often in the second part.
Two. You don't have to like it to accept it. Acceptance just means you stop fighting what already is.
Three. Fighting reality is a fight you always lose. Spend that energy on your response instead.
Four. Amor fati — love your fate. Don't just tolerate what happens; use it as material.
Five. Ask only: given that this is true, what's the wisest next move? Then take it.
Acceptance isn't giving up. It's putting your strength where it can actually change something.
